hints.text: Average 1² through 6² to obtain fair value.
The sum of the first six squares is 91.

solution.setup: The six payoffs are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, and 36 dollars.
solution.reasoning: Their mean is 91/6≈15.17. A $2-wide whole-dollar market centered near this value is $14 bid and $16 ask, which brackets fair value.
solution.finalAnswer: Fair value $91/6≈$15.17; one valid quote is $14 at $16.
solution.sanityCheck: The value must lie between the square of the mean, 12.25, and the maximum payoff, 36.

keyInsight: Price the expected payoff first; only then choose a spread around it.
recognitionCues: A random payoff and a requested quote call for expected value plus spread construction.
commonMistakes: Squaring the expected die roll instead of averaging squared outcomes.
followUps: What changes if customers know whether the roll exceeds 4?

source.notes: Original variant of a publicly reported interview family associated with Jane Street, Optiver.

title: Quote the Square of a Die
problem: A contract pays the square of a fair six-sided die roll in dollars. Find its fair value, then give a whole-dollar bid and ask exactly $2 apart that bracket the value.
